source_title: Frequently Asked Questions About Language Use

double_count_rule: Do not substitute deaf, hearing-loss, disability, or ACS English counts for ASL users.
recommended_use: Record a measurement gap; no numeric ASL-US input.
limitations: A Census working paper additionally explains that edited ACS data combine ASL write-ins with English.

source_locator: Knowledge of languages; American Sign Language; denominator 36,328,480

recommended_use: Direct Canada-specific ability/knowledge audience under the Census definition.
limitations: Not primary language, daily use, native language, or interpreter need; sample estimate and rounded output.

limitations: Main language only; ONS cell-key perturbation applies.

source_title: Scotland's Census 2022: ethnic group, national identity, language and religion
double_count_rule: Do not add to England/Wales/Northern Ireland main-language counts as a UK user total; definitions differ.
recommended_use: Broad Scotland can-use audience; retain separately from main-language counts.
limitations: New question; includes hearing people, learners, family members, and occupational users; count and rate rounded.

source_title: CT0041 Main language: sign language by religion
source_locator: British sign language row; table population usual residents age 3+

measure_label: Knows how to use Libras among people with hearing difficulty
source_publisher: Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE)
source_title: Pesquisa Nacional de Saude 2019: Ciclos de vida
source_locator: Libras section and Table 8; 153 thousand of 1.7 million; 9.2% (95% CI 7.3-11.6)
double_count_rule: Do not extrapolate to all Brazilians or add the 22.4% severe-hearing subgroup; that subgroup is nested in this population.
limitations: Excludes users outside ages 5-40 and users without reported hearing difficulty; approximate weighted counts.

source_publisher: DREES / ORS Pays de la Loire
source_title: Handicap auditif en France: apports de l'enquete HID 1998-1999
source_locator: Chapter V-2, PDF p. 75: approximately 119,000 users
double_count_rule: Use 119,000 once; do not also add its 44,000 and 75,000 components.
recommended_use: Qualified historical LSF-context user measure; preserve survey wording and exclusions.
limitations: Old survey; excludes blind people; wording is generic sign language rather than a language-code item.

source_title: Bericht der Bundesregierung zur Lage von Menschen mit Behinderungen
source_locator: PDF p. 51-52; approximately 100,000 dependent on interpreters
double_count_rule: Never treat as a DGS-language population and never add national deaf/hearing counts.
recommended_use: Interpreter-service need context only; exclude from signer totals.
limitations: Association estimate, dated, interpreter dependence differs from DGS ability or use.

measure_label: Uses sign language or sign interpretation as communication means
source_publisher: Japan Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
source_title: Communication support materials drawing on the FY2006 survey
source_locator: PDF p. 4: 343 thousand adults; 18.9%; approximately 65 thousand
double_count_rule: Do not label as a population-wide JSL count and do not add the 22,000 registered interpreting-service users, a nested service subset.
recommended_use: Restricted sign-mediated communication need proxy; exclude from named-language totals.
limitations: Does not distinguish JSL, signed Japanese, direct signing, or use through an interpreter; dated survey definition.

source_title: AI sign-language translation data annotation enables accessible information
double_count_rule: Never treat the hearing-impaired count as CSL users; it may include oral-language users and people needing captions or other supports.
recommended_use: Broad need context and deployment rationale only.
limitations: Submitted deployment case, not a population survey; no signer definition or compatible denominator.

measure_label: Hearing disability share among persons with disabilities
source_publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
source_locator: Census 2011: 2.68 crore persons with disabilities; 19% hearing disabilities
double_count_rule: Do not multiply this disability rate into an ISL-user count; hearing disability and ISL use are not equivalent.
recommended_use: Policy context only; preserve the ISL-user measurement gap.
limitations: Old disability census; no ISL ability, use, home-language, or native-language question.

source_title: 2021 Census All persons QuickStats and LANP dictionary
source_locator: Language used at home: Auslan; national value 16,242
double_count_rule: Do not add to broader Auslan ability estimates; one-response home use omits users selecting another language or using Auslan only outside home.
limitations: LANP non-response 5.7%; small random perturbations; not all users or native signers.

source_title: 2023 Census place and ethnic group summaries; Languages spoken quality statement
source_locator: Total New Zealand population column: NZSL 0.5%, count 24,678
double_count_rule: Do not sum with other language responses; a person may report up to six languages.
recommended_use: Direct NZSL ability/use audience under Census definition.
limitations: Random rounding; 85.3% current Census response, 8.8% historical responses, 0.4% deterministic derivation, 5.4% statistical imputation.

source_locator: Knowledge of languages; Quebec Sign Language; denominator 36,328,480
double_count_rule: Do not add to ASL or other language knowledge; multiple languages may be reported.
limitations: Not primary language, daily use, native language, or interpreter need; sample estimate and rounded output.

measure_label: Irish Sign Language used at home
source_title: Census 2011 Profile 8: Our Bill of Health
source_locator: Irish Sign Language section and Table B: 2,590
double_count_rule: Do not add the disability/hearing-impaired subgroups; they are nested within the 2,590 total.
limitations: Old Census; home-use question does not count every IrSL user; acronym kept as IrSL to avoid confusion with Indian Sign Language.

measure_label: Uses sign language among people with hearing disability
source_title: EDAD 2020: Utilizacion de la lengua de signos por sexo y edad
source_locator: Absolute table 51628: total hearing disability 1,230.0 thousand; uses sign language 27.3 thousand
double_count_rule: Do not assign the full count to one named language and do not add its age strata.
recommended_use: Direct generic sign-use need in a restricted population; not a named-language count.
limitations: Excludes hearing family members, learners, and interpreters; language identity is not distinguished.

measure_label: Independent Indigenous sign language; no defensible current user denominator

source_locator: announcement body: confirmation of uniqueness and independent-language status
double_count_rule: Do not substitute ASL, Deaf-population, or hearing-loss counts for Hawaiʻi Sign Language users.

limitations: Identity evidence does not supply a current user count or educational-material demand estimate.
